details:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Our project, Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, is an interactive virtual space exploration experience developed using PictoBlox. It takes learners on a simulated astronaut mission to explore space and understand black holes.

The project features two animated astronaut characters who guide learners through a space adventure using character movements, timed dialogues, and storytelling. During the mission, the astronauts encounter a mysterious dark object and investigate whether it is a dark planet or a black hole. Through their conversations, learners discover important facts about black holes, including their extremely powerful gravity, how light cannot escape from them, and why they do not have a solid surface.

Benefits and Intended Impact: The project makes space science easier and more interesting for young learners. It encourages curiosity, scientific thinking, creativity, and an interest in astronomy. It also introduces students to basic coding concepts through an enjoyable learning experience.

Tools and Technologies: We used PictoBlox, block-based programming, animated sprites, space-themed backdrops, motion blocks, event blocks, control blocks, and dialogue blocks. No external hardware is required.

Creativity and Design Considerations: We combined astronaut animation, storytelling, space visuals, and educational information to create an engaging virtual mission. Our team considered age-appropriate explanations, simple language, visual appeal, character interaction, and the sequence of activities to make the experience easy to follow and enjoyable for students.
